newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq shares decline further in cautious trade.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq shares decline further in cautious trade.

text.p: Nasdaq shares slipped further Monday amid weakness in technology shares and general caution ahead of Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's speech on Tuesday, traders said.

The Nasdaq composite index slipped for the third consecutive session, losing 11.75 points or 0.76 percent to close unofficially at 1536.24. Declining issues beat gainers 2457 to 1915 on total volume of 538 million shares.

"There's more to be cautious about today than to be excited about. People are still cashing in on last week's gains and they're waiting on the sidelines for which direction things will go after IBM and Greenspan," one trader said.

Microsoft Corp continued to fall after its fourth quarter earnings, released last Thursday, only modestly beat Wall Street expectations. Microsoft, the most active Nasdaq issue, dropped 4-9/16 to 135-15/16.

Investors were skittish about technology stocks ahead of International Business Machines Corp's earnings, traders said. After the market closed, IBM posted second quarter earnings of $1.46 a share, surpassing the Wall Street consensus estimate of $1.42 a share.
